newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-WMC proceeds with fertilizer project.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-WMC proceeds with fertilizer project.

text.p: Mining giant WMC Ltd said on Thursday it would proceed with a A$650 million project to produce phosphate fertilizers in Queensland.
WMC said the mine and processing facilities at Phosphate Hill, in northwest Queensland, would produce one million tonnes a year of high analysis ammonium phosphate fertilzers.
Construction was expected to start in early 1997, with production by late 1999.
"The Phosphate Hill resource, which containes two billion tonnes of phosphate rock...is a world class phospate deposit," WMC said.
Agreements had been finalised for the supply of natural gas and sulphur dioxide, which are needed for the processing and production of fertilizer.
Fertilizer would be transported by rail to Townsville.
WMC said the project would produce diammonium phosphate and monammonium phosphate, allowing the replacement of fertilizers which are currently imported.
Import replacement would save about A$230 million from Australia's balance of payments, it said.
WMC has been marketing high analysis fertilizers in south-east Australia for the past 10 years through its wholly owned subsidiary Hi-Fert Pty Ltd.
Fertilizers produced at Phosphate Hill would also be marketed through Hi-Fert, it said.
Product not sold within Australia would be exported to South-East Asia and other Pacific markets.
